stories.title: IndiGo's Q2 loss narrows to Rs 1,879 crore as fuel costs jump 67%
stories.summary: InterGlobe Aviation, IndiGo's parent, reported a Q2 FY27 net loss of Rs 1,879.1 crore, narrower than Rs 2,582.1 crore a year ago, as revenue rose 25.9% to Rs 23,363.8 crore. Excluding currency effects, the loss was Rs 723.7 crore against a profit last year.

stories.title: IndiGo says fares will have to rise
stories.summary: IndiGo is considering higher fares and a capacity review as aviation fuel costs surge, Storyboard18 reports. CEO Willie Walsh said the airline would have to pass on at least part of the increase, given limited scope for further cost cuts. 'We have no choice,' he said.

stories.title: Airlines push back on Mumbai airport's T1 shutdown
stories.summary: The Airline Operators Committee has asked for a phased redevelopment of Mumbai's Terminal 1, warning that a full shutdown before new capacity is ready could disrupt operations. Adani-run MIAL plans demolition from April 2027 and asked airlines for relocation plans by 3 November.

stories.title: Emirates and Air France-KLM are wary of moving to Navi Mumbai
stories.summary: MIAL wants to shift about five million passengers a year to Navi Mumbai by March 2027 for Terminal 1 work. Akasa, IndiGo and Air India have moved some international flights, Mint reports, but Emirates and Air France-KLM have raised concerns about the new airport's infrastructure.

stories.title: Mumbai airport will close both runways for six hours on 19 November
stories.summary: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport will suspend operations on both runways for six hours on 19 November for post-monsoon maintenance, Gulf News reports. UAE travellers flying to or from Mumbai are advised to check schedules with their airlines.

stories.title: Pune airport tops India in passenger satisfaction
stories.summary: Pune Airport ranked first among 16 Indian airports in the July to September Airport Service Quality survey by the Airports Authority of India and ACI, scoring 4.98 out of 5, Urban Acres reports. That leaves 0.02 for the queue at security.

stories.title: Bengaluru airport teams up with KPMG on a GenAI platform
stories.summary: Bangalore International Airport Limited has partnered with KPMG in India to build a generative AI platform for airport operations. It is meant to automate routine processes, analyse large datasets for predictive insights and support real-time decision-making across BIAL's systems, ET Infra reports.

stories.title: Air India Express adds Abu Dhabi to Amritsar and resumes Goa flights
stories.summary: Air India Express has launched direct flights between Abu Dhabi and Amritsar and resumed services to Goa, Travel Radar reports. Both began on 25 October and run three times a week from Zayed International Airport.

stories.title: IndiGo looks for more money beyond the ticket
stories.summary: IndiGo's ancillary revenue per passenger rose to Rs 590 in the September quarter from Rs 525 in the previous quarter, Inshorts reports. The airline sees room to grow paid add-ons, premium offerings and its loyalty programme. The seat is just the starting price.

stories.title: Air India extends its Saudi Arabia flight suspension to 14 November
stories.summary: Air India and Air India Express have extended the suspension of flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam until 14 November amid unrest in West Asia, the Times of India reports. IndiGo and Akasa Air have also suspended some Saudi routes.

stories.title: SpiceJet's Jaipur to Dubai flight runs more than 21 hours late
stories.summary: Passengers on SpiceJet's Jaipur to Dubai flight, scheduled for Friday evening, were still waiting on Saturday after the departure time was changed three times, Bhaskar English reports. They were told the flight would likely leave by 4 pm on Saturday.

stories.title: Southwest skips Dallas' new third airport
stories.summary: McKinney National Airport opens to passengers from mid-November as Dallas' third major airport, but Southwest Airlines will not fly there. CEO Bob Jordan told WFAA it 'didn't really work', Simple Flying reports. Avelo will be the only operator for now.

stories.title: Croatia Airlines posts a record nine-month loss
stories.summary: Croatia Airlines lost 64.7 million euros in the first nine months of 2026, more than triple the 20.9 million euros a year earlier, EX-YU Aviation reports. Operating revenue rose 8% to 221.2 million euros, while costs grew faster.

stories.title: Amadeus breach exposed data of about 92,000 JAL customers
stories.summary: Japan Airlines says unauthorised access to Amadeus' passenger service system between August 2023 and September 2026 exposed data on around 92,000 customers. About 2,000 had passport numbers and contact details exposed. Amadeus notified JAL of the breach on 23 October.

stories.title: JetBlue creditors hire advisers over debt worries
stories.summary: A group of JetBlue creditors holding about $2 billion in bonds due 2031 and a $742 million first-lien loan has hired PJT Partners and Akin Gump, Simple Flying reports. The move does not mean JetBlue has filed for bankruptcy or agreed to restructure.

stories.title: Air Canada reviews long-haul routes as fuel bites
stories.summary: Air Canada is reviewing its network and pace of growth as high fuel costs persist into next year, and has already cut more than two points of planned capacity growth from the first quarter of 2027, Aviation Week reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: United eyes its first flights to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan
stories.summary: United Airlines may launch flights to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, based on CEO Scott Kirby's comments on a recent podcast, Simple Flying reports. Kirby confirmed that a fellow United executive recently visited both countries.

stories.title: Delta adds Austin to Bentonville flights from March
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines will fly once daily between Austin and Bentonville from 7 March 2027, Simple Flying reports. It will be Delta's fifth destination from Northwest Arkansas National Airport, as the airline keeps growing in Austin.

stories.title: FlyArystan joins IATA
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's low-cost airline FlyArystan has joined the International Air Transport Association, the Astana Times reports. IATA represents more than 370 airlines in over 120 countries, accounting for nearly 85% of global air traffic.

stories.title: Flying Blue wins best rewards programme for a third year
stories.summary: Loyalty experts point.me named Air France-KLM's Flying Blue the best airline rewards programme for the third year running on 30 October, AeroTime reports, ahead of a top 10 dominated by US airlines. The field was narrowed from 59 programmes to 33.

stories.title: Discover Airlines will add A350-900s from 2027
stories.summary: Lufthansa Group's Discover Airlines will add A350-900s in 2027 in a fleet renewal plan, with the first four coming from sister carrier Lufthansa and nine more from 2029, FlightGlobal reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Air Congo to fly 787s through a MIAT wet lease
stories.summary: Mongolian airline MIAT has agreed to supply widebody capacity to Air Congo, the DRC-based carrier, which will introduce Boeing 787 service through the wet-lease arrangement, FlightGlobal reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Why Delta brought back the Boeing 747
stories.summary: Delta Air Lines operated the Boeing 747 again after an 18-year absence, and Simple Flying traces the decision to a major merger and an evolving network strategy across the Atlantic and Pacific. The jumbo first flew on 9 February 1969.

stories.title: Airbus delivers 547 jets in nine months and backlog tops 9,300
stories.summary: Airbus delivered 547 commercial aircraft from January to September, up from 507, as revenue rose 7% to 50.6 billion euros and net income rose 36% to 3.587 billion euros. It plans to raise A320 Family production to 75 a month.

stories.title: United's CEO says Boeing and Airbus lack pressure to build new jets
stories.summary: United CEO Scott Kirby says Boeing and Airbus have little incentive to develop clean-sheet aircraft because they dominate the market, and has called for a third major manufacturer, Aviation A2Z reports. United has invested in blended-wing startup JetZero.

stories.title: American Airlines takes four Airbus deliveries in one week
stories.summary: American Airlines took delivery of three A321neos and one A321XLR in seven days, Simple Flying reports, as it prepares for domestic and international growth. The airline expects another four Airbus deliveries before the end of 2026.

stories.title: Archer and ITA Airways plan air taxis for Italy
stories.summary: Archer Aviation and ITA Airways signed an agreement on 30 October to explore an eVTOL network linking Italian cities. Archer says its Midnight aircraft could reach central Rome from Fiumicino in under 10 minutes. ITA's CEO Joerg Eberhart called it 'an important step'.

stories.title: Joby and Beta fly side by side across Tampa Bay
stories.summary: Joby Aviation and Beta Technologies opened Florida's eVTOL Integration Pilot Program with flights from St. Petersburg to Tampa International in about 20 minutes, AIN reports. The route retraces the world's first scheduled airline flight in 1914, which took 23 minutes.

stories.title: Why Dubai may get Joby and Archer air taxis before the US
stories.summary: The UAE has inspected Joby and Archer aircraft in person and is likely to be the first place the two operate air taxi services, possibly this year, according to a Motley Fool piece on Yahoo Finance. Approvals are still required there.

stories.title: Dubai South signs for a wide-body MRO centre
stories.summary: Dubai South has agreed a new airside plot at Mohammed bin Rashid Aerospace Hub with Phoenix Aviation for a wide-body MRO, cabin modification and cargo conversion centre. It includes a 35,000 square metre hangar for three wide-bodies, with completion planned for early 2029.

stories.title: Embraer's E2 gives the Airbus A220 some company
stories.summary: Over 500 Airbus A220s are flying with operators including Delta, JetBlue and airBaltic, Simple Flying notes, but Embraer's E-Jet E2 series is competing for the same buyers. Embraer has delivered over 150 E2s to airlines such as Porter, KLM Cityhopper and Azul.

stories.title: Korean Air's aerospace arm eyes 777X work
stories.summary: Korean Air Aerospace Division is exploring opportunities to build aerostructures for the Boeing 777X as it anticipates resource reallocations between Boeing's commercial and defence units, Aviation Week reports from Busan. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: AAIB blames crew and controller lapses for Goa runway incursion
stories.summary: The AAIB found that the crew of Air India Express flight AXB-1109 at Goa acknowledged only a taxi instruction and missed the order to hold short of Runway 08, Business Today reports. The controller also did not insist on a full readback.

stories.title: Co-pilot made mandatory for Char Dham helicopter flights
stories.summary: Helicopters on Char Dham routes must now carry a co-pilot, decided at a meeting of the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority and DGCA officials on Saturday, PTI reports. It follows Friday's crash near Joshimath in Chamoli district that killed six people.

stories.title: How the AAIB will investigate the Joshimath helicopter crash
stories.summary: The AAIB will investigate Friday's crash of a Trans Bharat Aviation helicopter flying from Badrinath to Dehradun, in which all six people on board died, the Hindustan Times reports. The probe will follow the Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules, 2025.

stories.title: Akasa Air jet suffers a tail strike at Kolkata
stories.summary: Akasa Air flight QP 1925 from Ahmedabad carried out a go-around at Kolkata and landed safely, with all passengers disembarking. A post-flight inspection found the tail had touched the ground, the airline said. The aircraft is parked for a detailed inspection, the Economic Times reports.

stories.title: Pilots' body asks DGCA to suspend flights into West Asia conflict zones
stories.summary: The Airlines Pilots' Association of India has written to DGCA asking it to suspend operations into high-risk conflict zones in West Asia and require disclosure of valid insurance cover. It said it first raised the issue with the regulator on 18 March, ET Infra reports.

stories.title: FlyersRights sues the DOT over delay cost rule
stories.summary: FlyersRights has petitioned a US appeals court over a DOT rule it says shifts meal and hotel costs during disruptions from airlines to passengers. The rule moves 10 disruption types, including some unscheduled maintenance, out of the airline-controlled category. The DOT cites the 2024 FAA Reauthorization Act.

stories.title: Clearance mix-up sends four jets across a JFK runway
stories.summary: Poor coordination between controllers allowed four jets to cross a runway at New York's JFK in front of a departing Swiss A330, which aborted its take-off roll, FlightGlobal reports. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: PAL Airlines plane loses a wheel on landing in Wabush
stories.summary: A wheel came off PAL Airlines Flight 901 seconds after landing in Wabush, Labrador, captured on video by a CBC producer on board. The landing was smooth, passengers taxied in normally and no injuries were reported. The cause is yet to be determined.

stories.title: FAA ends single-pilot exemptions for older Citation jets
stories.summary: The FAA has ended single-pilot operations exemptions for legacy Cessna Citation 500 series jets, granted since 1984, AeroTime reports. Models from the Citation I to the Encore+ must now always fly with a trained second-in-command pilot.

stories.title: FAA reviews SpaceX plan for up to 456 Starship launches a year
stories.summary: The FAA has opened a public review of SpaceX's plan to raise launches at Boca Chica from 25 a year to as many as 456, and landings from 50 to 912, KRGV reports. SpaceX has launched three times from Starbase this year.

stories.title: Air India's Amravati flying academy gets DGCA approval
stories.summary: DGCA has issued a certificate of approval to the Air India Flying Training Academy at Amravati's Belora Airport, the Hindustan Times reports. MADC's Deepak Kapoor said it expected the academy to start operations as early as the first week of November. The approval came on Friday.

stories.title: India has 15% women pilots, against about 5% globally
stories.summary: Women make up about 15% of India's pilots against about 5% globally, the civil aviation minister said in August, Mid-Day reports. DGCA data counted 1,767 women among 11,775 pilots at six major airlines. The piece profiles Dr Harpreet A De Singh, India's first woman airline CEO.

stories.title: Goa plans a drone pilot training centre at Cacora ITI
stories.summary: Goa's skill development directorate has invited bids for a drone remote pilot training centre at Cacora Government ITI, estimated at Rs 1.26 crore. It will have two DGCA type-certified training drones, two flight simulators and a 3D printer, digitalgoa reports.

stories.title: New light-sport rules widen what entry-level US pilots can fly
stories.summary: The FAA has extended the privileges of sport pilot certificate holders, so pilots with the most basic credentials can fly a much wider range of aircraft, Simple Flying reports. The certificate was introduced in 2004 to make aviation easier to enter.

stories.title: Unleaded avgas will cost pilots more than the pump price suggests
stories.summary: General aviation is working to replace 100LL leaded avgas ahead of a US federal target of 2030, Simple Flying reports. A fuel costing under a dollar more per gallon can add thousands of dollars to an annual flying budget. The lead goes, the bill stays.

stories.title: Mooresville pilot receives the FAA's Wright Brothers award
stories.summary: Clifford Frost of Mooresville received the FAA's Wright Brothers Master Pilot Award on 23 October, presented by FAA inspector Michael Moran at his home, the Mooresville Tribune reports. It recognises more than 50 years of exemplary flight experience.

stories.title: Young Eagles flights give Alabama students a first taste of flying
stories.summary: Volunteer pilots with EAA Chapter 1358 flew Houston County students from Dothan Regional Airport on Friday through the free Young Eagles programme, WTVY reports, as the teens explored a future in aviation.
